title: Bone Press — Stedelijk Exhibition Wall
description: A museum-poster title slide channeling Wim Crouwel's Stedelijk discipline — one enormous condensed headline crashes the top edge over a bone-paper field, answered only by tiny mono exhibition-date meta at the foot. No images, no ornamentation: type is the architecture.
philosophy: This template exists because most slides labelled 'brutalist' merely swap a font and call it done, leaving comfortable proportions and decorative padding untouched. It commits instead to the full austerity of postwar Dutch institutional print: two type sizes, one hairline, and nothing else permitted on the canvas. It is built for speakers who believe a headline at 240 points is a complete argument — not a container waiting to be softened. Hospitality, warmth, and visual entertainment are explicitly out of scope.
goodFor: Mid-century graphic design or architecture retrospective title slides
Art history and design-theory lecture openers
Single-statement keynote titles for design-literate or academic audiences
Brand identity presentations where typographic restraint signals credibility
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews with multiple data hierarchies
Product launch decks requiring lifestyle photography or iconography
Content-dense slides with more than two levels of textual information
Audiences likely to read visual austerity as lack of effort or polish
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a load-bearing wall in a postwar Dutch museum: one colossal typographic gesture at the top, then disciplined silence for the rest of the canvas. Composition is intentionally top-heavy and confrontational — the headline does not frame content, it IS the content, an assertion rather than a container. Mood is cold institutional authority channeling mid-century exhibition graphics: no warmth, no entry point, no ornamentation permitted to soften the impact. Avoid any decorative impulse — the hairline rule is the only structural concession; everything else is type against field.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed canvas with zero top margin — the condensed headline block crashes flush against the upper edge, its cap-height grazing the border with no breathing room above. A 12-column grid underlies the layout; the headline spans all 12 columns at maximum compressed scale, occupying roughly the top third of the canvas. A single hairline rule drawn edge-to-edge separates the headline zone from the vast, empty bone-paper field below. Tiny mono exhibition-date meta is baseline-pinned to the bottom margin: deck topic or section label flush left to column 1, a minimal folio reference anchored flush right.

examples.promptCore: An exhibition wall text panel translated to a slide: one dominant typographic statement arrests the eye before reading begins, its scale making it architectural rather than informational. A single hairline separates it from a sparse category label above — the only hierarchical signal permitted. The right margin holds a narrow column of tiny mono annotation, cool and clinical. The mood is postwar Dutch institutional discipline: rigorous, unapologetic, with no hospitality toward the viewer's comfort.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid, hard left bleed; the primary content statement occupies cols 1–8 in an oversized condensed weight that dominates the vertical field. A single hairline rule separates a compact category or section label at top from the statement body below — the only hierarchical device on the canvas. Cols 9–12 hold a narrow mono annotation column, running top-to-bottom like a museum catalog gloss. Page folio sits bottom-right, outside the grid boundary, at caption scale; no padding softens any edge.
